newsitem.title: USA: MBf USA to get $6.75 million in stock sale.
newsitem.headline: MBf USA to get $6.75 million in stock sale.

text.p: MBf USA Inc said Tuseday it will receive $6.75 million in proceeds from the sale of 2,500,000 unregistered shares of its common stock to Wembley Rubber Products of Malaysia.

MBf said it will used the proceeds for working capital, to introduce new products, to reduce debt and to introduce advanced technologies in its 70 percent owned powdered latex glove manufacturing factory in Indonesia.
Wembley is the principal supplier of powder-free latex business gloves to MBf.

In addition, Wembley also will purchase all of MBf USA's Class A common stock, or 1,252,538 shares, from its majority shareolder, MBf International Ltd, at a price of $5.00 per share, or a total of $6.27 million.
MBf International will retain its 1,682,275 shares of common stock of the company.

MBf said the Class A common stock allows the holder to designate a majority of the members of the company's board of directors and represents 29 percent of the common stock, assuming no new shares are issued.
As a result, Wembley will be able to elect new Class A directors and a majority of the Class B directors, and will hold 55.1 percent of the common stock.
MBf's subsidiary is American Health Products Corp (AHPC).
"With its $6.75 million capital infusion, Wembley has demonstrated confidence in AHPC and will expand its business partnership," Edward Marteka, president, said in a statement.

"AHPC will now be in a stronger position than ever before with this new partnership, for it combines the superior sales and marketing strength of American Health Products Corporation with Wembley, among the largest powder-free glove producers in Malaysia," he added.
